record.one_liner: HubSpot is a CRM and marketing/sales platform with a REST API for CRM objects and developer tooling.
record.auth_notes: Docs list two authentication methods: OAuth (public apps) and private app access tokens (sent in the Authorization header). Private app tokens are treated as api_key.
record.access_notes: A standard HubSpot account can be free or paid and is where apps and private app tokens are created. Free-tier API limits were seen only in a search snippet, not a fetched page, so the free-tier claim is unverified. Developer test accounts are a separate 90-day trial.
record.api_notes: Docs say all REST APIs are available via private app token or public app OAuth token. Breadth is a judgement call based on CRM object coverage; not separately verified.
record.blocker_notes: Remote MCP requires the new Developer Platform and a user-level OAuth app with read scopes for the CRM objects needed. Legacy private apps can no longer be created, so new builds go through the developer platform.

evidence.quote: There are two ways to authenticate calls to HubSpot’s APIs: OAuth, and private app access tokens.
It can be free or paid, and is used as your production environment.
All REST APIs are available to query via a private app access token or public app OAuth token.
New legacy apps cannot be created.
